paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take with you, friend. The Sadducees had a clever puzzle, seven brothers and one widow, and it still missed the whole point. Jesus tells them why: "You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God." (Matthew 22:29) They knew the words well enough to build a trap out of them. They just didn't know the God behind the words. And I get it, because I once thought I had the whole story figured out from the back of a junk drawer!

So what did Jesus do? He didn't just fix their math. He said that in the resurrection, people "will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven." (Matthew 22:30) The life God has coming is bigger than anything our questions can hold. When our picture of God is too small, we end up asking small questions about a big promise. Don't shrink the promise to fit your puzzle, baker.

Then Jesus takes them to what God said: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." Then He says, "He is not the God of the dead, but of the living." (Matthew 22:32) That means the people who belong to God are held by a God who is alive. So read your Bible to know Him, not just to win the argument. That's why my ovens stay warm, and the crowds were astonished at His teaching (Matthew 22:33). Stay hungry for it!
